# refactor(cli): introduce the composition owner and executable

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the error-ownership issue, and builds on it. The next slices (moving the GitHub code,
then the application API) build on this one and also edit `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`.

## What

The `jig` command starts from one clearly named place that does nothing except assemble the
program and start it. Commands, help and installed usage behave exactly as before.

## Why

Startup and wiring currently live inside the GitHub feature folder, which makes that folder an
extra layer above the command line. A dedicated starting point keeps wiring separate from command
handling and application behavior.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Composition", "Dependency lint", and the `composition` row of "Target responsibilities".

- `src/integrations/github/cli.ts` composes the full CLI and starts the executable. Move executable
  startup and command composition to `src/composition/main.ts`, keeping the realpath check that
  makes installed symlinks work. Importing builders or the module must not start a command.
- `package.json`: `bin.jig`, `main` (`./dist/integrations/github/cli.js`) and `scripts.dev`
  (`tsx src/integrations/github/cli.ts`) point at the new executable. Update path-sensitive tests,
  `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts`, and `docs/installation.md` line 52.
- Composition may import `app`, `cli`, `adapters`, `config`, `observers`, `ports` and `domain`.
  It only chooses implementations, constructs them and starts the executable. In this slice it
  still calls the existing app container. Leave the container itself alone; a separate spike
  decides how it changes.
- Dependency Cruiser: add `composition` to `productionModules` in `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`.
  Add the rules "only composition imports `src/cli/` from another owner" and "no other owner
  imports `src/composition/`". The rules cover type-only imports, re-exports and literal dynamic
  imports. `scripts/validate.ts` may keep using CLI parsing helpers; do not let the source-only
  rule break it. Extend `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` with fixtures that accept composition
  importing CLI and reject an adapter, app or nested file importing CLI or composition. Each
  rejection must fail under the named rule, not because of an incidental cycle.
- `src/integrations/github/command.ts` remains a CLI-side command file; the next slice moves it.
  If a temporary edge from `cli` to `integrations` is needed, record it in the PR and do not add a
  forwarding module.

## Done when

- [ ] `node dist/composition/main.js --help` and `node dist/composition/main.js github implement --help`
      work after `npm run build`, and a symlinked executable starts.
- [ ] A spec imports the composition builders without starting a command.
- [ ] Fixtures prove the new rules, including type-only, re-export, dynamic, nested and
      disconnected offenders.
- [ ] Executable paths in `package.json`, the tests and the docs point at `src/composition/main.ts`.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/57
